title: Procurement & Legal: LLM Terms - Initial Handover
summary: Intro handover between AE/SE and Everwell procurement/legal. Covered MSA/DPA redline priorities, SLA expectations (p99 latency targets, uptime), deployment modes (hosted vs private/VPC), KMS/HSM keying options, pricing pathways (reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go) and pilot acceptance criteria. Agreed to circulate redlines + security pack and schedule legal deep-dive next week.
action_items: Alex Mercer - Send annotated MSA/DPA redline matrix by 2025-08-22
Samir Patel - Share pilot benchmark spreadsheet + suggested load profile by 2025-08-25
Claire Zhou - Provide security pack (SOC2, ISO attestations, pen test summary) by 2025-08-22
Ibrahim Khan - Provide expected token volumes and peak qps for pilot by 2025-08-23
next_steps: Redwood to circulate redline/response doc and security pack
Procurement to confirm pricing approval path and finance owner (Jordan to share)
Technical pilot to start after sign-off on DPA (target week of 2025-09-08)
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2025-08-20 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: see metadata above

Summary (auto): quick handover; legal/procurement orientation around MSA/DPA, KMS and pricing.

[00:00] Alex Mercer (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. I'm Alex from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Quick round robin?
[00:18] Maya Rhodes (General Counsel): Hi, Maya here. I'll be driving legal redlines.
[00:22] Jordan Blake (Procurement): Jordan - procurement, finance approvals for vendor onboarding.
[00:27] Ibrahim Khan (Platform Eng): Ibrahim - I'll lead the pilot on infra side.
[00:32] Samir Patel (SE): Samir here - I'll handle the technical scope and run the benchmark tests.

[01:10] Alex: Cool. Purpose today is an initial handover — surface the legal/procurement asks we've been hearing, align on SLA/pricing expectations, and lay out next steps for a pilot. We'll be pretty candid about tradeoffs, e.g., hosted vs dedicated, and keying options.

[02:05] Maya: From legal perspective top priorities are: data processing addendum alignment, clear egress/residency commitments, KMS/HSM support or customer-managed keys, and audit log retention. Also curious about indemnity and subprocessor lists.

[02:48] Samir: On the KMS side, we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS integration. For on-prem/private we can do an HSM-backed key path but there are config timelines — usually a 2-week prep for key rotation and integration.

[03:25] Sasha (Customer Security): Quick question — does Redwood write logs that contain prompts or outputs? We need to know retention and masking options.

[03:40] Claire (Redwood): We do retain operational logs for troubleshooting; however we have options to disable retention for production workloads and a KV-cache prefix mask. We'll share the security pack with exact retention windows, and there's an option for no-logs for dedicated private deployments.

[04:55] Jordan: Pricing — high level, procurement will need a committed spend path to get better unit costs. We prefer reserved capacity if it gives predictable monthly burns. How does Redwood price reserved vs on-demand?

[05:25] Alex: Two main pricing lanes: hosted usage-based (per-token) and Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit for GPU pools). Dedicated gives a lower per-token rate for steady throughput and SLA. We can model blended pricing for the pilot.

[06:12] Ibrahim: For the pilot we need target p99 latency and peak qps numbers to validate. Also is there a rollback if model quality regressions occur?

[06:32] Samir: Target p99 we see depends on model and config. On our curated medium model we can hit p99 < 400ms for 512 tokens on dedicated capacity, on hosted it can be variable. We usually ship a performance profile; will include sequence length distributions in the pilot sheet. And yes, rollouts can be pinned or set to fallback if quality drops.

[07:10] Maya: On the MSA/DPA — our legal team will want to limit liability and tighten data use clauses. Any standard exceptions you can't accept?

[07:40] Alex: We aim to be flexible but some clauses (like absolute zero liability) are hard. We can accept most DPA redlines around subprocessors and residency with appropriate scoping. We'll send an annotated redline matrix rather than a full MSA rewrite to speed things up.

[09:05] Speaker 1 (Customer ops): Are there any export control or cross-border transfer fees we should plan for?

[09:22] Claire: There can be egress costs depending on region; we'll include egress mapping. For EU data residency we can run in EU regions or a private VPC to satisfy residency requirements.

[10:15] Sasha: What about auditability? We need tamper-evident logs and an audit trail for who accessed keys.

[10:30] Samir: If you run private VPC with customer-managed keys, you own the key access logs. On hosted we provide audit logs with RBAC and we can integrate with your SIEM via log forwarders. HSM gives stronger tamper-evidence — we'll include that option in the security pack.

[12:00] Jordan: On procurement cadence, we need a pricing sheet and a one-page cost model for finance to review. Also the MSA needs to go through our legal intake by 08/29 to hit the September budget window.

[12:30] Alex: Understood. We'll aim to hit those dates. We'll also propose pilot acceptance criteria so finance can see the ROI ladder.

[14:10] Ibrahim: For the pilot, our staging environment is air-gapped-ish; we need to confirm network connectivity and whether Redwood can support a temporary peering or site-to-site VPN.

[14:28] Samir: We support both site-to-site and cloud VPC peering; the private deployment package has a connectivity checklist. There's some firewall config on both sides. We'll share the connectivity playbook.

[16:00] Maya: A redline ask — data deletion clause with a 30-day purge for test data and 90 days for production logs. Also we need a subprocessor list and a notification window for changes.

[16:30] Claire: We can commit to subprocessor notice windows and a data deletion SLA. The 30/90 windows are doable for hosted with a retention toggle; for dedicated we can coordinate immediate deletion on provisioned nodes but there are nuances during backups. We'll document exceptions.

[18:20] Jordan: Financial questions: If we go reserved, what's the minimum term? Can we do a 6-month pilot reserved tranche?

[18:45] Alex: We usually do 12-month reserved contracts for committed discounts, but we can offer a 3-6 month pilot commit with pro-rated pricing to bridge. I'll flag finance to provide a pilot-specific term sheet.

[20:00] Ibrahim: Are there egress fees if we pull embeddings back into our environment?

[20:15] Claire: Embedding egress is typically counted as part of token egress; region-to-region transfers may have fees. We'll include examples in the cost sheet.

[22:05] Maya: Indemnity — we need to see scope around IP claims and a carve-out for our use of customer data.

[22:35] Alex: We can discuss narrow indemnity windows; our legal team will propose language that is common in enterprise SaaS deals.

[24:00] Speaker 1: Sorry quick clarification — what are the failure modes? If production latency spikes do you automatically failover to another region or model?

[24:18] Samir: We have smart routing and fallback policies. For Hosted we can route to a lower-cost variant or another region; for Dedicated there's capacity fallback options. We can set an automated policy that fails over to a cheaper model or queuing if latency crosses SLO thresholds.

[26:00] Jordan: We will need an SLA with credits tied to monthly uptime and p99 latency thresholds. What do you offer?

[26:20] Claire: Our enterprise SLA includes monthly uptime target (99.9% for dedicated), and latency SLOs are documented per model and workload. Credits scale with severity. We'll include the SLA template.

[28:30] Maya: About subprocessor transparency — we need a way to reject certain subprocessors. Is that supported?

[28:50] Alex: We publish a subprocessor list and we have an escalation flow; for critical subprocessors we can operate under a transparency/notification model and discuss mitigations.

[30:00] Ibrahim: Technical acceptance for the pilot — our criteria will be: functional parity for NLU tasks, p99 below X ms (we'll share X), and throughput to support peak qps. Also a regression tolerance for hallucination rates below Y% — will Redwood help instrument that?

[30:28] Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and eval hooks; we can integrate your prompt sets and run evaluations during pilot. We'll instrument hallucination metrics and build a quality dashboard.

[33:00] Jordan: On the approvals path, procurement needs a one-pager and the SOW with scope. Can Redwood produce a pilot SOW and milestone table?

[33:20] Alex: Yes, we'll draft a pilot SOW with milestones tied to acceptance criteria. We'll also propose a two-phase pilot: benchmarking + integration, then production-like load test.

[35:40] Maya: Also please include a breach notification SLA — 72 hours seems to be our baseline.

[35:58] Claire: We normally have a 72-hour notification window for incidents and a 30-day remediation cadence for moderate issues. Security pack will detail incident response contacts.

[38:10] Ibrahim: For network peering there are certs and IP allowlists — any support from Redwood?

[38:25] Samir: We'll assign a deployment engineer during the pilot to help with peering and allowlists. That will be in the SOW.

[40:00] Jordan: Ok sounds good. Timelines: procurement wants price model and redline response by next Friday (08/22) to review for budget window. Legal deep-dive next Wed (08/27). Pilot ideally to start first week of September.

[40:22] Alex: We'll target that. Quick check — any absolute deal breakers we should know about?

[40:35] Maya: Two potential blockers: 1) inability to use customer-managed keys for production; 2) unconstrained subprocessor changes without notice. If those are unacceptable, we may pause.

[40:55] Claire: Both are addressable — CMK in private deployment and notification windows for subprocessors. We'll detail implementation and timelines.

[42:10] Alex: Great. We'll circulate: 1) annotated MSA/DPA redline matrix, 2) security pack, 3) pilot SOW and cost model, 4) benchmark spreadsheet. Expect initial pack by Friday 08/22.

[44:00] Jordan: Who will be the point on Redwood side for legal?

[44:12] Alex: I'll be the commercial lead; Lee Nguyen (Redwood legal) will join the deep-dive. I'll copy Lee on the redline doc.

[45:25] Maya: Ok thanks. One last ask — can you include sample audit logs so our SIEM team can validate fields?

[45:40] Samir: Yes, we'll attach sample logs and field mappings.

[46:10] Alex: Recap of next steps and owners — Alex to send redline and pricing, Samir to send benchmarks and logs, Claire to send security pack, Ibrahim to share volumes. Legal deep-dive scheduled. Thanks everyone.

[46:50] Meeting ends.
